record.paper_title: Slices of Brownian Sheet: New Results, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let B = {B(s,t)}_{s,t ≥ 0} be a d-dimensional two-parameter Brownian sheet, and for each s > 0 consider the zero set of the slice t ↦ B(s,t), namely {t > 0 : B(s,t) = 0}. When d ∈ {2,3}, does there exist an event of probability one on which, simultaneously for every s > 0, this slice zero set B^{-1}{0} ∩ ({s} × (0,∞)) is a finite set?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1. Suppose d ∈ {2 , 3}. Is it true that outside a single null set, B−1{0} ∩ ({s} × (0 , ∞)) is a finite set for all s > 0?
Theorem 1.2. If d ∈ {2 , 3}, then the following holds outside a single P-null set: dimH(B−1{0} ∩ ({s} × (0 , ∞))) = 0 for all s > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B=\{B(s,t)\}_{s,t\ge 0}$ be a $d$-dimensional two-parameter Brownian sheet; that is, $B$ is a centered Gaussian random field taking values in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with independent coordinates, each coordinate having covariance $\mathbb{E}[B_i(s,t)B_i(s',t')] = \min(s,s')\,\min(t,t')$. Fix $d\in\{2,3\}$. For each $s>0$, consider the zero set of the slice $t\mapsto B(s,t)$, namely
$$Z_s := \{t>0 : B(s,t)=0\} = B^{-1}\{0\}\cap (\{s\}\times(0,\infty)).$$
Determine whether there exists a single event of probability one on which, simultaneously for every $s>0$, the set $Z_s$ is finite.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on zeros of the Brownian sheet (including a 2024 preprint resolving a different question of Khoshnevisan, about projections preserving Hausdorff dimension of the zero set) does not appear to settle the finiteness of slice zero sets for d∈{2,3}. The strongest available related result is that the slice zero sets have Hausdorff dimension zero almost surely simultaneously in s, but no source found establishes (or refutes) finiteness. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Zeros of the Brownian Sheet
status_evidence.snippet: Answers a question of Khoshnevisan about projections of the zero set preserving Hausdorff dimension; does not address slice-finiteness.
status_evidence.claim: A recent advance resolves a different Khoshnevisan open problem on the Brownian-sheet zero set, leaving the slice-finiteness question apparently untouched.
